options.say: I print the stage schedules! I know where everyone goes. Give me a story and I'll give you a coach.

options.text: What do you know about Mott?

exchange.speaker: frame
exchange.line: Everything! I wrote most of it.

exchange.speaker: frame
exchange.line: Some of it was told to me.

options.text: Do you have a photograph of him?
options.say: I have the photograph of him.

repeats.say: That's how it's spelled in Providence, is it? Extraordinary place.
I'll fix it in the next edition.
The type's worn. It's not my fault the letter B has opinions.

options.text: Does Fanshawe ever leave his office?
options.say: For funerals! Every one. Front pew, black gloves, a wreath the size of a cartwheel. I print the notices, and he's the only man in town who reads them.

options.text: I need a funeral notice printed.

exchange.speaker: frame
exchange.line: 'MEMORIAL FOR E. PIKE, LATE. ALL WELCOME. REFRESHMENTS.' I've added refreshments. It doubles the turnout.

options.text: Have you ever been in the Liar's Assay?

exchange.speaker: frame
exchange.line: Once! Fellow told me he'd found a nugget shaped exactly like the President, and I said—

exchange.speaker: frame
exchange.line: 'So did four men this month. It is a popular shape.' I printed it. Front page. He moved to Sacramento.

options.text: A piano tuner bought the worst claim in the district on purpose.

exchange.speaker: frame
exchange.line: Don't tell me. It's better not knowing.

exchange.speaker: frame
exchange.line: Vessel took the Tuesday coach to Fiddler's Gulch. Two days out, if the road holds, and the road never holds.

options.text: There's a raccoon in my hole with a name.

exchange.speaker: frame
exchange.line: A NAMED raccoon. Sir, you are a wellspring.

exchange.speaker: frame

options.text: What did you print about Vessel leaving?
options.say: 'BELOVED CITIZEN ANSWERS CALL OF COMMERCE.' He owed me for six advertisements. The headline was cheaper than forgiving the debt.
A correction! We run those in the spring.

repeats.say: Persistent AND punctual-minded. I may do a profile. How do you spell it?

options.text: I've taken enough of your time. I'll be taking more later.

opening.speaker: frame
opening.line: An obituary. For the piano man.

opening.speaker: frame
opening.line: Everyone knew him. He was— —he was the only man in town who fixed anything.

options.say: The truth. It's an obituary. There are rules.

exchange.speaker: frame
exchange.line: He never gave me one worth having.

exchange.speaker: frame
exchange.line: I invented better. He never complained. That was the quote, probably.

options.text: I am going to leave now, in a dignified manner.
